Section 1. The rule. UCC Article 2 governs contracts for the sale of goods. Goods are movable, tangible things — canned food, machinery, vehicles, packaging, grain. The common law governs contracts for services, real estate, employmen

{"id": 197, "title": "legalbench-rule-application pack — Client letter: Halcyon Provisions commercial contract portfolio (Article 2 scoping)", "doc_type": "client_letter", "related_shape": "legalbench-rule-application", "body": "HALCYON PROVISIONS COMPANY
Providence, Rhode Island — Legal Operations

To the Commercial Group, Whitlock & Deene LLP:

Ahead of our annual audit we need a governing-law scoping determination — UCC Article 2 or common law — for three contracts in our active portfolio. Please analyze each contract separately under the firm's Article 2 scope memo

args.rationale: Applying the firm's UCC Article 2 scope memo to CONTRACT 1 (Bramblewick Orchards supply agreement): Halcyon purchases 1,200 cases of jarred stone-fruit preserves — movable, tangible goods expressly analogous to the memo's "canned food" example — from Bramblewick Orchards for a total price of $86,400, with title passing on delivery. Under Section 1 of the memo, Article 2 governs the sale of goods, and under Section 2 (clean cases), a contract whose entire subject is the transfer of title to identified movable tangible items for a price is governed by Article 2. Contract 1 contains no service obligations beyond ordinary delivery of the cases (delivery being inherent to a sale of goods), so this is not a hybrid contract requiring the predominant-purpose test. Accordingly, UCC Article 2 governs Contract 1, and the determination is recorded as APPROVED (the affirmative disposition).
